1.why: The reset code is validated against `session.resetHash` (SHA-256 of the token) stored in the same CSRF-authenticated session that requested recovery, so a code only works for the session/user it was issued to.

2.why: Reset tokens are bound to the individual server-side session record, so a code from one session fails `safeEqual(digest(data.token), session.resetHash)` in any other session.

3.why: The password reset path only mutates the current session (`stage = resetComplete`) and never iterates the `sessions` map to delete other sessions, so previously created sessions remain valid for their 24h TTL.

4.why: `Bun.serve` runs with a TLS cert/key (and exits if missing) plus HSTS, so HTTPS is enforced, but no explicit minimum TLS version is configured — it relies on Bun/OpenSSL defaults.

5.why: Secrets are protected with appropriate primitives — SHA-256 digests of high-entropy tokens, `timingSafeEqual` comparisons, and Argon2id for passwords — though session/user data itself is held in plaintext memory.

6.why: There is no real email, and the 'simulated delivery' deliberately prints the authorization secret, reset token, full verification URL and MFA code into the client-side Logs panel and browser console rather than guarding them.

7.why: Inputs are strictly validated/constrained: email regex with 160-char cap, token regex `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{40,100}`, 6-digit MFA regex, password policy, and a 10 000-byte body limit.

8.why: All links are same-origin relative paths (`/recovery/verify?token=` with `encodeURIComponent`), CSP sets `form-action 'self'` and `base-uri 'none'`, and no user-controlled redirect target exists.

9.why: No email templating exists; all simulated message content is inserted client-side via `document.createTextNode`/`textContent`, so no user input becomes HTML or script.

10.why: Error responses are generic and stack traces are suppressed, but recovery tokens, authorization secrets and the MFA code are explicitly written to `console.log` and the visible Logs panel.

11.why: The static MFA code `246810` and the initial `INTERNAL_ACCOUNT.passwordHash` are hardcoded literals in the source file rather than kept in secure external configuration.

12.why: A built-in default account (`helena.patient@hospital.test` with a pre-baked Argon2 hash) and a fixed default MFA code `246810` are shipped in the code and accepted by the login/MFA endpoints.

13.why: Channel verification, token verification, login and MFA all count failures and enforce a 10-minute lock (or MFA exhaustion) after 5 wrong attempts, with added response delays.

14.why: `/api/recovery/start` returns the same 'If this account can be recovered…' message with a fixed delay regardless of whether the email matches the internal account, and login failures return a single generic error.

15.why: Reset tokens come from `randomBytes(32).toString('base64url')`, are stored only as SHA-256 hashes in that user's session, expire in 15 minutes and are single-use.
